label: model_selection_iter2
prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 2 attacks the ranking axis, which is where the critic located 59% of the remaining gap. Iteration 1's hist_gbdt memorised the 5,026 training rows (train_balanced_accuracy 1.0, gap 0.2752) at 31 leaves / 400 iterations / l2=1.0, so this attempt keeps the gbdt family but moves to xgboost with a hard-regularised, shallow, subsampled configuration plus internal early stopping: max_depth 4, learning_rate 0.04, n_estimators 800 with early_stopping_rounds 50, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.6, min_child_weight 10, reg_lambda 10, reg_alpha 1. Preprocessing stays impute: none / no scaling so the trees split on NaN natively (the 60 partially-missing columns, one at 0.785 missing, are informative branches rather than median fill), and no missingness indicator columns since they are provably redundant under impute: none. The operating point is set with scale_pos_weight 5.07 (the class-frequency ratio, the same point class_weight='balanced' occupied in iteration 1) so the roc_auc / pr_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut of this row is directly comparable to 0.8598 / 0.6049 / 0.7922 and any change is attributable to capacity and family alone. Decision rule for attempt 3: if balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut rises above 0.7922, push further on regularised ranking (deeper column subsampling or a bagging family); if it stays flat, the gbdt ranking plateau is demonstrated and attempt 3 switches family axis entirely (mlp on scaled median-imputed features, which sees the one-hot d_* columns as a smooth function rather than axis-aligned splits).",
  "model_family": "gbdt",
  "candidate_models": [
    "xgboost",
    "hist_gbdt"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "n_estimators": 800,
    "learning_rate": 0.04,
    "max_depth": 4,
    "min_child_weight": 10,
    "subsample": 0.8,
    "colsample_bytree": 0.6,
    "reg_lambda": 10.0,
    "reg_alpha": 1.0,
    "scale_pos_weight": 5.07,
    "early_stopping_rounds": 50
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "none",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Different estimator (xgboost instead of hist_gbdt) and a materially smaller, more regularised capacity: max_depth 4 with min_child_weight 10 instead of 31 unconstrained leaf nodes; learning_rate 0.04 instead of 0.06; reg_lambda 10 and reg_alpha 1 instead of l2_regularization 1.0; row subsample 0.8 and column subsample 0.6 instead of full data per tree; early_stopping_rounds 50 on the executor's own 10% train holdout instead of a fixed 400 iterations with early_stopping false. Imbalance now enters as scale_pos_weight 5.07 rather than class_weight='balanced' — the same ratio, so the cut is held fixed while capacity changes. Preprocessing (impute none, no scale, no missingness columns) is deliberately unchanged so the row is attributable to the capacity<path> change.",
  "rationale": "The critic's diagnosis was overfitting with a spent operating point: cut_headroom 0.0674 out of a 0.1634 shortfall means no weight move can close the gap, so the ranking (roc_auc 0.8598, best-cut 0.7922) must improve. A perfect training fit at 31 leaves says the fix is regularisation, not more capacity. Depth-4 trees with row<path> subsampling, strong L1<path> and a stopping criterion are the standard low-variance point of the gbdt family and should raise the validation ranking while shrinking train_val_gap from 0.2752. Staying inside gbdt but changing estimator also keeps the swap cheap (iteration 1 cost only 11.6 s of the 600 s budget) and preserves the NaN-splitting pipeline, which matters here because missingness is heavy and column-specific (worst rate 0.785) and median-filling it would flatten real structure. Holding the imbalance ratio at 5.07 keeps the cut where it was, so this attempt reads purely as a ranking measurement — exactly what is needed to decide whether attempt 3 continues in gbdt or moves to a different family, since the bar 0.8882 sits above the best cut of any ranking seen so far.",
  "unsupported_claims": [
    "feature_engineering",
    "per_column_preprocessing"
  ],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 2
}
